title: dynamic-deprioritization-for-kv-heavy-requests-to-prevent-starvation
author: Marisol Vega
description: Motivation: In production we observed tail-latency spikes and near-starvation of small non-KV requests when KV-heavy requests dominated continuous-batching queues. This PR introduces a dynamic deprioritization policy that detects long-running KV-dominant queues and reweights request admission and scheduling to reduce starvation while preserving batch efficiency. Approach: add token-based aging for fairness, per-queue KV-pressure heuristics, transient deprioritization buckets for KV-heavy groups, and a kernel-hint flag to prefer low-overhead kernels for short requests. Also introduce a soft release policy in the KV pin manager to proactively free pinned cache entries when a queue is deprioritized. Implementation highlights: 1) scheduler/continuous_scheduler: new "deprioritize_score" computed from recent kv_ratio, avg_service_time, and age, used to adjust admission priority and timeouts; 2) scheduler/aging_token: lightweight token bucket that guarantees forward progress for aged requests; 3) kernel/kernel_selector: expose "prefer_small_request_kernels" hint; 4) kv_cache/pin_manager: add background eviction signal when deprioritization fires to avoid long-term pin accumulation; 5) observability: new metrics (scheduler.deprioritize_events, scheduler.kv_pressure_ratio, scheduler.age_starved_count) and dashboards; 6) tests: synthetic kv-heavy and mixed workloads included in perf harness. Results: in lab kv-dominant 75/25 mix, p95 latency for non-KV small requests dropped 18% and p99 dropped 23% with <5% throughput loss for KV throughput; reduction in observed starvation incidents from 14/day to 1/day in canary. Rollout plan: gated rollout via feature flag with 1%, 10%, 100% progression and realtime metrics alerts. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] perf tests, [x] e2e smoke, [x] observability, [x] docs, [x] migration guidance. Related: ENG-1298 (scheduling fairness), ENG-1303 (kv pin release).

review_comments: Ava Patel: Nice approach. Two concerns: how do we avoid oscillation where deprioritized queues reappear and then flip-flop? Can we add hysteresis?
Marisol Vega: Added hysteresis window and decay factor to deprioritize_score; documented behavior in code comments and tests.
Jared Nguyen: Kernel hint is neat; please ensure it's opt-in per deployment. Also run the matrix with large-sequence workloads.
Marisol Vega: Kernel hint behind feature flag and empirically tested with seq_len 512/1024; no regression observed.
Ethan Cho: Suggest adding an integration test that simulates pin saturation and ensures the soft release reduces pin count.
Marisol Vega: Added an integration test (tests/integ/pin_release_saturation.py) and a CI perf job to run it on schedule.
Ava Patel: Approving after addressing oscillation and integration test.
Ethan Cho: Approved with no further comments.
release_notes: Improves continuous batching fairness by dynamically deprioritizing KV-heavy queues to prevent starvation of small requests. Adds observability metrics and a kernel hint for small requests. Rollout behind feature flag.
notes_for_backport: Small risk change but affects scheduling logic. Backport to release/2026-02 required for high-volume customers impacted by KV starvation. See migration guidance in docs/observability/scheduler-deprioritization.md.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover score calculation, aging tokens, and kernel hint toggles. Perf harness shows p95 improvements on mixed workloads; canary run (2% traffic) ran for 48h with telemetry showing reduced starvation incidents. CI added scheduled perf job for regressions.
changelog_entry: scheduler: add dynamic deprioritization for KV-heavy queues (reduces tail latency for small requests, feature-flagged)
additional_context: This PR complements previous weighted-queue and timeout-guard efforts but takes an empirical approach: detect KV pressure and adapt admission/scheduling rather than purely static caps. The soft release in pin_manager is conservative to avoid premature cache churn.
